mission: Advance genomic science and its application to biomedical discovery, with major programs in single-cell genomics, functional genomics, and disease genetics.

featured.position: Computational Biologist, Single Cell Genomics (Satija Lab)
featured.description: Full-time computational biology role in the Satija Lab developing statistical methods and open-source software for single-cell genomics, with applications in cancer immunology and developmental neuroscience.
featured.responsibilities: Develop computational methods for single-cell genomics datasets; contribute to open-source software packages; assist with data analysis/interpretation across lab projects; help manage lab servers and computational infrastructure; document and present results to the lab.
featured.qualifications: BS or MS in bioinformatics, computer science, biology, biochemistry, or similar; strong programming in R, Python, and BASH; Linux experience; strong written/verbal communication. Preferred: statistics or ML training; NGS, functional genomics, or human genetics exposure. Salary range listed as $65,000–$85,000.

mission: End cancer for life through patient care, research, and education — including basic and translational lab science across Sloan Kettering Institute and MSK clinical programs.

featured.description: Onsite research technician role in the Philipp Niethammer Lab studying how cells sense physical stress, using zebrafish, human cells, microscopy, genetics, and molecular biology.
featured.responsibilities: Prepare and maintain lab equipment, solutions, and assays; perform techniques such as CRISPR screening, flow cytometry, sterile mammalian tissue culture, transfection, fluorescent imaging, and tissue processing; conduct animal studies (injections, tissue/fluid collection, euthanasia, zebrafish handling); record/analyze data and assist peers on ongoing projects.
featured.qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in biology/life sciences; experience with tissue culture and molecular biology; comfort working with zebrafish larvae or adults (monitoring, genotyping, behavioral scoring, tailfin amputation); attention to detail, protocol adherence, teamwork. Location: NYC; 37.5 hours/week onsite; pay range listed ~$26.77–$40.05/hour.

companyType: HHMI research campus (nonprofit basic science institute)
mission: Solve fundamental problems in biology by bringing scientists and tool-builders together — including new imaging chemistry and microscopy methods that enable multimodal and super-resolution biological imaging.

featured.position: Postdoctoral Scientist — Lincoln Lab (fluorophores / super-resolution imaging)
featured.description: Postdoc in the Lincoln Lab designing and characterizing next-generation fluorophores for multimodal, whole-organism, and/or super-resolution imaging challenges.
featured.responsibilities: Design and execute multistep synthetic routes for new small-molecule fluorophores and ligands; develop high-throughput spectroscopic assays and characterize photophysical profiles; apply dyes in live/fixed imaging contexts; may train into single-molecule imaging, immunofluorescence, super-resolution methods, or related techniques as projects require.
featured.qualifications: Ph.D. in chemistry, physics, or a related physical/life science field; hybrid background in photochemistry and/or chemical biology with strong organic chemistry grounding; hands-on organic synthesis of fluorophores or light-sensitive substances; experience with computational chemistry tools (e.g. Gaussian, Orca). Spectroscopy, assay development, molecular docking, or fluorescence microscopy are assets. Janelia Postdoc 00 compensation listed at $74,200.

companyType: HHMI research campus (nonprofit basic science institute)
mission: Advance systems neuroscience and method development — including how neural circuits generate collective behavior and social cognition in experimentally tractable model systems.

featured.position: Postdoctoral Scientist — Schulze Lab (systems neuroscience / behavioral ML / VR)
featured.description: Postdoc integrating custom hardware/software with computational analysis to probe neural circuits underlying collective behavior and social cognition, including VR paradigms in Danionella.
featured.responsibilities: Build and apply virtual-reality behavioral paradigms with the lab’s VR specialist; develop/execute experiments on inter-individual differences and social behavior circuits; use multi-animal tracking and behavioral classification to study latent structure and create brain–behavior maps; integrate software-hardware systems with analysis pipelines.
featured.qualifications: Ph.D. in neuroscience, computer science, engineering, or a closely related field; hybrid background bridging software-hardware integration, computational/ML skills, and systems neuroscience; experience building or working with complex behavioral rigs (e.g. VR). Genuine interest in neural bases of social/collective behavior. Janelia Postdoc 00 compensation listed at $74,200.

mission: Accelerate research by making high-quality plasmids, viral vectors, and related research materials accessible to scientists worldwide — plasmids are the core portfolio that enables viral vectors, antibodies, and new formats.

featured.description: Senior manager role owning day-to-day execution of Addgene’s plasmid product portfolio — segmentation, catalog health, roadmap delivery, and launch execution — in partnership with the Director of Scientific Product Management (Watertown, MA; hybrid).
featured.responsibilities: Track and report plasmid portfolio performance (revenue growth, margin, catalog health) against Annual Operating Plan targets; set/hit targets for adoption, market penetration, and retention across academic/biotech/pharma segments; identify gaps and recommend pricing, positioning, promotional, or product-mix changes; own roadmap delivery and launch execution for the plasmid portfolio.
featured.qualifications: Senior product/portfolio leadership background suited to a scientific materials business; ability to translate scientific insight into commercial results with urgency and clear outcomes ownership. Salary listed $130,000–$155,000 plus benefits; hybrid at Watertown, MA headquarters. Confirm full requirements on the posting.

mission: Use functional genomics and gene-editing technologies to understand how genetic variation shapes gene expression and cellular phenotypes relevant to disease.

featured.description: Postdoc mentored by Dr. Neville Sanjana on functional genomics and gene editing — e.g. Cas13 noncoding RNA profiling in human neurons, in vivo CRISPR screens, protein design of new editors/cell therapies, or massively parallel enhancer/noncoding perturbations.
featured.responsibilities: Plan and carry out research independently; develop and execute a functional genomics / genome technology project; write up and present findings regularly; contribute experimentally and/or computationally depending on background (the role can be tailored toward wet-lab scientists building computational skills or computational geneticists building experimental expertise).
featured.qualifications: PhD or MD-PhD; prior research experience in molecular biology, biochemistry, computational biology, and/or functional genomics; first-author publications expected. Strong fit for candidates eager to connect human genetic variation to cellular/tissue phenotypes with cutting-edge genome technologies.
